name: Minimum Degree of Majority
proof: The $1$-inclusion graph is the $n$-cube on the base coordinates, except that every edge from layer $t=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ to layer $t+1$ is removed because it changes the majority bit.  A vertex in layer $t$ has degree $t$, while one in layer $t+1$ has degree $n-t-1$; all other vertices retain degree $n$.  The minimum is therefore $\min(t,n-t-1)=\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$.
